title: timeline_*.json — curated real-history event catalogs
$comment: Shape validation only. Two further checks run in the schema suite and cannot be expressed here: every effectId must exist in the effect palette registry, and every magnitude must sit inside that effect's declared cap.

severity.$comment: Drives effect scaling. Be conservative — a catalog where everything is a 4 has no dynamic range.

headlineBrief.$comment: A prompt input, not published prose. Factual and terse — the LLM writes the article.

issuePressure.$comment: Which issues this event pushes the city toward, per axis, in [-1, +1]. An unstated issue is simply not pressed. Optional and additive: TimelineCatalogLoader.ReadIssuePressure has read this key since it was written, and an event without it carries IssuePosition.Centre — which is why adding it here does NOT bump schemaVersion. SupportedSchemaVersion is a hard equality, so a bump would be a rejection rather than a migration, and it would break the one direction that already works (an old build reading a new file). The wave-3 precedent is engine_tuning, which bumped because a section gained a REQUIRED property. Direction is a claim about the argument, never about a party: AffinityEngine dot-products this against each party's platform and has no idea who governs.

pressureAxis.$comment: One issue axis of an issuePressure. TimelineCatalogLoader rejects anything outside [-1, +1] as IssuePressureOutOfRange, so the bound is enforced twice deliberately: the schema catches it at authoring time with a path, the loader catches a file the schema suite never saw.
